title: Certificate Authority
body:
A Certificate Authority is a trusted third party that signs a server's TLS certificate, vouching that whoever controls that certificate really does control that domain. Your operating system and browser ship with a list of root CAs they trust; during the [[TLS Handshake]] the browser checks that the server's certificate chains up to one of those roots, hasn't expired, and matches the hostname it's connecting to.

This is the *authentication* leg of [[HTTPS]] — the part that stops an impostor from simply pretending to be the real server. Note that the CA is a machine belonging to neither you nor the destination, which is why compromised or careless CAs are a genuine systemic risk to the whole model.
